task.title: Harden the desktop main process's lifecycle paths
task.description:
Two pre-existing main-process issues surfaced by the review of "Let the sidebar collapse to a rail". Neither is that feature's bug, so they were left out of its diff.

## A failed theme save is an unhandled rejection

The `board:scheme` listener in `desktop/src/main/main.js` is an async `ipcMain.on` handler that nothing awaits. If `registry.setTheme()` rejects (a full disk, an unwritable userData directory), the rejection is unhandled in the main process and the user sees a Dark Mode switch that did nothing. The sidebar shortcut hook already catches and logs its own toggle; give this handler the same `.catch` with a `console.error` in the file's voice.

## The window is never let go of on close

`window` is never nulled and `boardViews` / `activeProjectId` survive a window close, because `main.js` has no `window.on('closed')`. On macOS, close the window and reopen it from the dock: `createWindow()` runs again, but `layout()` still iterates the stale board views and calls `setBounds` on views whose window is gone. A visible symptom on the sidebar branch: Cmd+B does nothing in the reopened window, because `toggleSidebar()` rejects inside `layout()` and the rejection lands in the console. Fix: on `closed`, null `window` and `chromeView`, close and drop every board view (or park them and re-add them to the new window, if keeping boards warm across a close is wanted), and reset `activeProjectId`.

## Verification

`npm run check` in `desktop/`, plus a manual run on macOS: close the window, reopen from the dock, open a board, press Cmd+B.
